citation.title: Perspectives in the clinical application of cephalometrics. The first fifty years

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1). Scan with no text layer: every value re-read on the page images (PDF pages 9, 10, 13, 16, 17, 21, 22, 23 = pp. 123, 124, 127, 130, 131, 135, 136, 137). a and b agreed on every mean of every table row (Tables 1-7, cue sheet items 1, 4, 5, 10 at age 15) and on every definitionMatch; checked on the images: Table 1 83/84/85/86/87, males 88/89/90 (first age printed indistinctly, read 3 from the cue sheet 'age 3 = 83°' and the 3-year step); Table 2 28/27/26/25/24, males 23/22/21; Table 3 yearly 19.0 ... 27.4 (3-17), males 28.0/28.6/29.2 (18-20); Table 4 4.5/3.8/3.1/2.4/1.7, males 1.0/0.3/-0.4; Table 5 age 3 'Unerupted', 9/12/15/18, males 21/24 printed beside ages 18 and 21, nothing beside 24; Table 6 122/124/126, males 128/130; Table 7 0/-1.25/-2.50, males -3.75/-5.00; cue sheet item 10 age 15 = -3.0 ± 2. Differences: (1) SD on the age rows only in b (facial angle has it in both): MP ±4, interincisal ±5, lower lip ±2 (all age rows) -> kept, ruling P7 (a cue-sheet SD stated at one age applies to every age row); U6-PTV ±3 -> kept, checked on p. 136, which allows a deviation of ±3 mm, Ricketts' clinical deviation, the same kind of ± as the cue sheet's (doubt noted in the report). Mandibular bend SD 4.7 at age 8 only (both). (2) #64 a = 2 ± 2, b = 1 ± 2.5 -> 2 ± 2 from p. 135 with clinicalTarget '+1 mm ± 2.5' (ruling P8 revised; both sentences confirmed on the p. 135 image). (3) source wording (prose) -> each row names its table, page and tabulated age. Cue sheet p. 124 read in full from the page image: every row legible (items 1-11); the row earlier OCR could not read is legible on the image, nothing omitted for it. Item 11 prints 'age 8 ± 22.0°', a misprint for '= 22.0°' (Table 3), no SD taken from it. Rulings applied: #27 0 ± 3 from p. 131 with the 2.5 note (owner 7 Oct); P7; P8; facial axis Pt-Gn to Ba-N 90 ± 3; centre 'ideal' on the SD-less clinical norms (convexity, mandibular bend except age 8; owner B-2), no centre where an SD is printed; scale not-stated (magnification-research.md); P34/P36 — no band-less rows beside age rows and no overlapping bands. Fix round 1 (2026-10-08, owner rulings R-1 and R-2, ruling P38): the merge's nearest-age bands were replaced by the printed ages ([a, a]); the set is ageRows 'interpolate', so a known age between two printed ages is interpolated linearly (mean and SD; no SD where only one of the two rows has one). The last printed men's row is a point, except the facial angle's age-24 row, open [24, 99] because p. 127 says the angle reaches about 90° by adulthood. Each men-only adult row has a women's copy with the same values (fromOtherSex 'M'), flagged 'other-sex-values'. No value changed: only ageBand, notes, the added women's rows and ageRows.

caveats: Ricketts' norms are clinical norms collected over the years from various studies and clinical findings (p. 131); no sample, n, sex split or film scale is given. Table 1's heading describes the facial angle's mean behaviour in an American (Californian) Caucasian population.

The adult rows (ages 18 and over) of Tables 1-7 are bracketed 'Males'. Owner ruling R-2 (8 Oct): adult women are compared with the men's values; each such row has a women's copy (fromOtherSex 'M'), flagged 'other-sex-values' with 'Ricketts prints adult values for men only' in the source line. Child rows are pooled.

Ricketts prints values at single ages (owner ruling R-1): exactly on a printed age the row is used as printed; between two printed ages the norm is interpolated in a straight line between them, flagged 'interpolated' and named in the source line (e.g. interpolated between Ricketts 1981's ages 6 and 9). An interpolated value is not one Ricketts printed: it assumes the change between his two ages is even, which his own rates (in each row's note) say it roughly is. Before the first printed age, or after a last row that does not hold through adulthood, the end row is used, flagged 'age-mismatched' (no extrapolation). Only the facial angle's age-24 row holds for every older age (p. 127). With the age unknown, a man or woman gets the age-18 row (the youngest adult row); with sex and age both unknown, the oldest pooled row (age 15), flagged 'age-mismatched' and said (the source line says the oldest printed row, 15 y, was used).

SDs: Ricketts' clinical deviations, stated once on the cue sheet (facial angle ±3°, mandibular plane ±4°, interincisal ±5°, lower lip ±2 mm) or in the text (U6 to PTV '±3 mm', p. 136), applied to every age row of the measurement (ruling P7). Mandibular bend: SD 4.7° at age 8 only (Table 3 caption); the other ages carry no SD. Convexity carries none.
#27 palatal plane: 0° ± 3° from p. 131 (owner ruling 7 Oct); the cue sheet (item 5, p. 124) prints 'Clinical norm = 0° + 2.5°'.

#64 lower incisor to A-Po: 2 ± 2 mm is the figure from studies of untreated normal dentitions (p. 135); Ricketts' own objective, +1 mm ± 2.5 mm (p. 135; cue sheet item 7), is the clinical target (ruling P8).
#30 facial axis: 90° ± 3° (cue sheet item 1; p. 123); does not change with growth on average (change 0° ± 1.5° each five years, p. 123).
Cue sheet item 11 prints 'age 8 ± 22.0°' for the mandibular bend: a misprint for '= 22.0°' (Table 3 gives 22.0° at age 8); no SD taken from it.
Table 5 (U6 to PTV): age 3 'Unerupted' (no entry); no value is printed beside age 24 (only 21 and 24 mm beside ages 18 and 21), so after 21 the age-21 row is used, flagged age-mismatched.
#71 upper lip to E line: no number; p. 137 places the ideal upper lip about 2 mm further behind the line than the lower lip. Not entered.

Cue sheet changes stated as a rate are in each row's note: facial angle +1° each 3 years; mandibular plane −1° each 3 years; convexity −0.7 mm each 3 years; U6 to PTV +1 mm each year; interincisal +2° each 5 years; lower lip −0.25 mm each year; mandibular bend +0.6° each year.

Not in the catalogue: the frontal analysis (cue sheet p. 139, Tables 8-10: nasal width, maxillary and mandibular width, intermolar and intercuspid width, midlines, symmetry), Table 11 (divine-proportion measures) and the fossa / true-porion position data (Figs. 7-8).
Film scale not stated (magnification-research.md); the mm rows are used as printed (assumed true size, owner M-2).
